insights_payload.analysis: [Agent-generated insight] Neither spark.sql.adaptive.enabled nor Databricks' dbx_autooptimizeshuffle is active. The job shuffles ~32 TB (shuffle_bytes_read=32.4 TB, shuffle_bytes_written=31.9 TB) across 1,054,430 tasks in 1,836 stages. Without AQE, Spark cannot coalesce small post-shuffle partitions or split skewed ones at runtime. The static 200-partition setting is the sole control over shuffle granularity, and it is demonstrably too coarse given the spill trend. Enabling AQE would allow Spark to dynamically right-size partitions per stage, reducing both spill pressure and scheduling overhead from the large number of tiny tasks observed in many stages.
insights_payload.evidence: aqe_enabled_param=null (not set), dbx_autooptimizeshuffle=false. shuffle_bytes_read=32,354,263,719,362 bytes (~32 TB), shuffle_bytes_written=31,907,717,800,806 bytes (~32 TB). num_spark_stages=1836, num_spark_tasks=1,054,430. Stage 1881 shows 3,911 tasks with median scheduler_delay of 511ms vs median executorRunTime of 32ms — scheduling overhead dominates many small stages. Stage 1867 (3,856 tasks) and Stage 1869 (200 tasks, 502 GB disk spill) illustrate the wide variance in partition sizing that AQE would address.
insights_payload.readable_name: [Agent] AQE Disabled on a High-Shuffle, Spilling Workload — Static Partition Count Cannot Adapt

recommendations.reason: HEALTH REMEDY — passes the health gate. Spill_ratio=0.084 (8.4% of I/O), chronic across all 15 runs (mean 6.9 TB spilled/run, trending +13.7%). AQE is NOT enabled (spark.sql.adaptive.enabled=not_set, dbx_autooptimizeshuffle=false), so spark.sql.shuffle.partitions is the direct, active lever — not a no-op. Current ratio: 200 partitions / 100 executors = 2.0 (flagged 'Low — hot partitions likely'). Each of the 200 reduce tasks must process ~32 TB / 200 = ~160 GB of shuffle data, far exceeding the per-slot execution budget (executor_heap=11.5 GB, off-heap=35.6 GB, 16 cores → per-slot budget ≈ (11.5 + 35.6) GB / 16 ≈ 2.9 GB). Raising to 800 partitions targets a ratio of 8 partitions/executor and reduces per-task shuffle data to ~40 GB / task, a 4× reduction in per-slot working set. Sizing arithmetic: target = max(200, shuffle_bytes / 128 MB) = max(200, 32,354 GB / 0.128 GB) = 252,768 — but that ceiling is impractical at 100 executors (scheduling overhead). The insight-suggested range of 800–1000 is the practical target: 800 gives ratio=8, well above the 'hot partitions' threshold of 5, and reduces per-task data to a manageable ~40 GB. Estimated saving: spill_ratio=0.084 × used_vcore_time=1,792,004s ≈ 150,528s of wasted vcore-time per run. Recovering ~50% of that (conservative, since more partitions reduces but does not eliminate spill) ≈ 75,264s/run. At ~20 runs/15 days → ~365 runs/year, saving ≈ 75,264 × 365 / 3600 ≈ 7,630 vcore-hours/year. Estimated_saving_fraction ≈ 0.084 × 0.5 × (used/allocated) ≈ 0.084 × 0.5 × 0.268 ≈ 0.011 of total allocated cost, but the spill also stretches wall-time and inflates all duration-integrated costs — the broader saving fraction is bounded by spill_ratio ≈ 0.07–0.08. NOTE: This is the ONLY executor-memory cluster change this visit (orthogonality). Insight ref=4 (enable AQE) is in the same executor-memory/partition cluster and is explicitly deferred to the next visit per the conflict resolution below.

insights_payload.suggested_action: Enable spark.sql.adaptive.enabled=true. On Databricks Runtime this also activates partition coalescing and skew join handling. Pair with the shuffle partition increase (insight 1) — AQE will coalesce upward from the higher baseline rather than being constrained by 200. Do not set both changes in the same deployment; apply the partition count change first, then enable AQE in the following run.

insights_payload.analysis: [Agent-generated insight] The cluster runs exactly 100 on-demand workers (clusterMinWorkers=clusterMaxWorkers=100) with dynamic allocation disabled. vcore_utilization is only 26.8% (used_vcore_time=1,792,003s vs allocated vcore_time=6,731,431s), meaning ~73% of paid compute is idle at any given moment. Because autoscaling is off and dynamic allocation is disabled, the cluster cannot shed idle executors between the many short stages (e.g. stages with 1–16 tasks running on a 1,600-vcore cluster). This is a cost pathology that is independent of the spill health issue — the cluster is structurally over-provisioned for the actual parallelism the workload can exploit at its current partition count. Note: the SQL rule already flagged over_provisioned_cluster_machines; this insight specifically identifies the mechanism (dynamic allocation disabled + fixed cluster size) and the interaction with the partition count fix.

insights_payload.analysis: [Agent-generated insight] Disk bytes spilled has increased monotonically from ~6.5 TB to ~7.4 TB over the last 15 runs (+13.7%) with no configuration changes. This is not a one-off event: the trend is directionally consistent across the full history window.
